title: Is FREQUENCY a comparative weight or an independent probability? The wiki calls it 'a comparative number', and E34 hinted at it — when seven suppressed species were restored, the OTHER cavern species fell 39 to 0 and 27 to 12 while an untouched control's held steady, which looks like crowding. The mix cannot separate the models: a ratio of independent probabilities tracks the frequency ratio too. So both arms hold the SAME 4:1 ratio at very different absolute levels — TROGLODYTE and ELK_BIRD at 100 and 25 against 4 and 1 — with every other species left at its natural frequency. NOTHING is zeroed: E35's first attempt isolated the pair by zeroing 81 species and hit the CREEPY_CRAWLER freeze (addendum 54). A season, two replicates each, tool disabled, cavern counts excluding the magma sea and underworld.
fork: Does cavern arrival volume depend on the absolute frequencies or only on their ratio — that is, can frequency compose an ecosystem rather than only switch a species off.

predictions.expects: the two species' SHARE of cavern arrivals rises sharply in the high arm at the expense of everything else, while total cavern arrivals stay about the same in both arms
the two species' own counts scale with their frequencies (roughly 25-fold between arms) while the other species' counts are unaffected, so the total rises in the high arm
the two species' counts do not track their frequencies; frequency is not a proportional lever at all

kill_criterion: unchanged totals with a shifted share makes frequency a comparative weight and an ecosystem-composition lever; totals rising with the absolute level makes it an independent per-species probability
culling: drop a replicate on any changed save

arms.name: high_4to1
pre: local sw=reqscript('seasonal-wildlife'); local cfg=sw.loadConfig(); if not cfg.initialized then sw.captureDefault(cfg) end; cfg.enabled=false; cfg.groups.enabled=false; cfg.ecology.enabled=false; sw.saveConfig(cfg); sw.disableSched(); local n=0; for _,cr in ipairs(df.global.world.raws.creatures.all) do if cr.creature_id=='TROGLODYTE' then cr.frequency=100; n=n+1 elseif cr.creature_id=='ELK_BIRD' then cr.frequency=25; n=n+1 end end; print(('e36: TROGLODYTE=100 ELK_BIRD=25 (ratio 4:1, sum 125); %d set, every other species left at its natural frequency'):format(n))

local function f(t) for _,cr in ipairs(df.global.world.raws.creatures.all) do if cr.creature_id==t then return cr.frequency end end return -1 end; local ur=df.global.world.world_data.underground_regions; local function depth(c) local r=ur[c]; return r and r.layer_depth or -1 end; local cav,deep=0,0; for _,u in ipairs(df.global.world.units.active) do if dfhack.units.isWildlife(u) and not dfhack.units.isDead(u) and not u.flags1.inactive then local r=u.animal.population; if r.cave_id>=0 then if depth(r.cave_id)<=2 then cav=cav+1 else deep=deep+1 end end end end; local cz=0; for _,u in ipairs(df.global.world.units.active) do if dfhack.units.isCitizen(u) and not dfhack.units.isDead(u) then cz=cz+1 end end; print(('e36: caverns=%d deep=%d citizens=%d trog=%d elk=%d day=%d'):format(cav,deep,cz,f('TROGLODYTE'),f('ELK_BIRD'),math.floor(df.global.cur_year_tick/1200)))
